reporting-org.narrative: Obodo Centre for Advocacy and Equal Rights

description.narrative:
The group counseling sessions hosted by Obodo have become a cornerstone of our mental health and community support initiatives, offering vital spaces for healing, reflection, and connection within the LGBTQ+ community. These sessions have been particularly impactful in providing much-needed emotional support in the wake of significant community losses and ongoing societal challenges.
One of the most poignant sessions was held on Trans Visibility Day, titled Immortalizing Fola Francis, held on Trans Visibility Day, which saw 78 attendees come together to discuss grief mechanisms, community building, and celebrate the life of Fola Francis, a cherished member of our community who tragically passed away in December 2023. This session provided a safe space for attendees to express their emotions, share their memories of Fola, and engage in collective mourning, which is often a vital step in the healing process for communities that face ongoing marginalization and loss.
The healing circle component of Yahaya’s "Art n Soul" initiative was another key offering designed to address mental health from a holistic perspective. There were 33 participants in the circle. The circle served as a communal space where individuals gathered to share their lived experiences, listen to others, and find solace in collective healing. The circle incorporated mindfulness practices, reflective dialogue, and emotional support, all of which contribute to a deeper sense of connection and understanding among community members..
In collaboration with UsTherapy, we also held group and ongoing private therapy sessions specifically for queer artists. These sessions, facilitated by Aanu Jide-Ojo MBPsS, are centered around The Cost of Creating as a Queer Artist, addressing the unique psychological and emotional challenges faced by queer creatives. The discussions provide a safe space for artists to explore issues related to identity, expression, and the often overwhelming pressures of creating art in a socio-political landscape that can be hostile to LGBTQ+ individuals. These sessions are invaluable in offering validation, coping strategies, and a sense of solidarity among participants. So far, there have been eight persons who attended individual therapy sessions and ten who attended a group therapy session during our Arist Connect weekend with the Queer Artist Fund cohort members and staff.
Additionally, we organized a transformative 2-day Grief & Somatic Healing session which had 38 persons in attendance. The healing session combined various holistic approaches to trauma recovery. Participants engaged in trauma-conscious yoga, embodied movement and dance, somatic experiencing, guided breathwork, and grief tending practices. This multifaceted approach allowed participants to reconnect with their bodies, release stored trauma, and process grief in a supportive and nurturing environment. The sessions were met with overwhelmingly positive feedback, with participants expressing deep gratitude for the opportunity to engage in such a comprehensive and healing experience.
Through these group counseling sessions, Obodo continues to address the complex mental health needs of the LGBTQ+ community, offering safe spaces for healing, strengthening, and community building in the face of adversity.
Expenditure to be carried out in the next year
